overview.historicalContext:
**Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness (Millennium Prize Problem)**

The Navier-Stokes equations describe fluid motion: $\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla)u = \nu\Delta u - \nabla p + f$ with $\nabla \cdot u = 0$. The Millennium Prize asks whether smooth solutions exist globally in 3D. Leray (1934) proved weak solutions exist; Ladyzhenskaya (1962/1969) solved the 2D case; Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg (1982) showed the 3D singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most 1. The 3D problem remains open after 90+ years.

This formalization is the largest single proof file in the gallery at 20,000+ lines across 110 parts, containing 1200+ definitions/theorems with 0 sorries. The 3D conditional result uses the NSAxioms structure (5 structure-encoded assumptions).
overview.problemStatement:
**Millennium Prize Problem**: In 3D, prove existence and smoothness of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for all smooth initial data, or provide a counterexample showing finite-time blowup.

**2D Result (PROVEN)**: Global existence and uniqueness holds because vortex stretching vanishes and enstrophy is bounded.

**3D Conditional Result (PROVEN)**: Under the NSAxioms structure (physical hypotheses), global regularity follows from Type I exclusion (ESS theorem) and Type II exclusion (stability analysis).

overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization has two main threads:

**2D (Complete)**: The scalar vorticity equation has no stretching term, so enstrophy $\int|\omega|^2$ satisfies $E' = -2\nu P \leq 0$. This gives global bounds, preventing blowup.

**3D (Conditional)**: Blowup is classified as Type I ($\|u\| \sim (T-t)^{-1/2}$) or Type II (faster). Type I is excluded by the ESS theorem (bounded ancient solutions are zero via Liouville). Type II is excluded by stability analysis ($\beta_{\text{eff}} \to 0$). Together: no blowup is possible under the NSAxioms hypotheses.

The file also develops extensive supporting theory across 40 parts.
keyInsights: In 2D, vortex stretching vanishes entirely, making enstrophy a Lyapunov function
The ESS theorem (2003) rules out Type I singularities via backward uniqueness for ancient solutions
All 35 original axioms were eliminated: proved from first principles, proved vacuously, or removed as dead code
The 3D conditional result uses the NSAxioms structure (not Lean axiom declarations), maintaining honest separation of assumptions
Liouville theorems for ancient solutions are the key to ruling out self-similar blowup
Koch-Tataru (2001) identified BMO^{-1} as the largest critical space for small-data global existence
The stationary Liouville critical exponent 9/2 vs the regularity exponent 3 measures the gap to solving the Millennium Problem
prerequisites: Partial differential equations (incompressible Navier-Stokes, vorticity formulation)
Functional analysis (Sobolev spaces, Leray-Hopf weak solutions, semigroups)

sections.title: Numerical Constants and Basic Inequalities
sections.summary: Parts I-II: Spectral gap, Faber-Krahn, concentration constants. Bernoulli inequality, exponential dominates polynomial, backward growth estimates.
sections.mathContext: Spectral gap $\lambda_1 \geq c_d / |\Omega|^{2/d}$ (Faber-Krahn). Bernoulli: $(1+x)^n \geq 1 + nx$. Growth: $e^x$ dominates $x^n$ for all $n$, i.e., $\lim_{x \to \infty} x^n / e^x = 0$.

sections.title: Ancient Solutions and ESS Theorem
sections.summary: Part III: Ancient solutions, bounded ancient solutions, Liouville theorem (bounded ancient = zero), ESS exclusion of Type I blowup.
sections.mathContext: Ancient solutions: defined for $t \in (-\infty, 0)$. Liouville: bounded ancient $\Rightarrow u \equiv 0$. ESS: Type I ($\|u\| \lesssim (T-t)^{-1/2}$) excluded by backward uniqueness.

sections.title: NS Solution Structure and Type II
sections.summary: Parts IV-VI: Solution envelope, blowup definition, Type II scenario, stability analysis, effective beta vanishing, Type II no-blowup proof.
sections.mathContext: Type II blowup: $\|u(t)\| (T-t)^{1/2} \to \infty$ as $t \to T^-$ (faster than Type I rate $(T-t)^{-1/2}$). Stability: effective parameter $\beta_{\text{eff}} \to 0$ excludes Type II singularities.

sections.title: NS Axioms and Main Theorem
sections.summary: Part VII: NSAxioms structure, Type II scenario construction, main global regularity theorem (conditional).
sections.mathContext: Main theorem: Type I excluded (ESS) + Type II excluded (stability) $\Rightarrow$ no finite-time blowup under `NSAxioms` (5 structure-encoded assumptions).

sections.title: CKN Concentration and Partial Regularity
sections.summary: Parts VIII-A through VIII-H: Concentration framework, K-ball analysis, tropical framework, CKN dimension, theta dynamics, closure, twin-engine stability.
sections.mathContext: CKN partial regularity: the singular set $\mathcal{S} = \{(x,t) : u \text{ not bounded near } (x,t)\}$ satisfies $\dim_H(\mathcal{S}) \leq 1$. Epsilon-regularity: if $r^{-1} \int_{Q_r} |u|^3 + |p|^{3/2} < \varepsilon$, then $u$ is regular at the center.

sections.title: 2D Global Existence (PROVEN)
sections.summary: Parts X, X-B: Complete 2D Navier-Stokes global existence and uniqueness. Enstrophy bound without axioms, exponential decay under Poincare inequality. The fully proved result.

sections.title: Gronwall, Leray-Hopf, Serrin
sections.summary: Parts XII-XIV: Gronwall stability, Leray-Hopf weak solutions (energy inequality, weak-strong uniqueness bootstrap), Serrin regularity criterion (2/p + 3/q <= 1).
sections.mathContext: Leray-Hopf: $\|u(t)\|^2 + 2\nu \int_0^t \|\nabla u\|^2 \leq \|u_0\|^2$. Serrin: $u \in L^p_t L^q_x$ with $2/p + 3/q \leq 1$ $\Rightarrow$ regularity.

sections.title: Turbulence and BKM Criterion
sections.summary: Parts XV-XVI: Kolmogorov K41 energy spectrum, Reynolds number scaling, BKM blowup criterion (vorticity controls regularity).
sections.mathContext: K41: $E(k) \sim \varepsilon^{2/3} k^{-5/3}$. BKM: $\int_0^T \|\omega\|_{L^\infty} < \infty$ $\Rightarrow$ no blowup at $T$.

sections.title: Weak-Strong Uniqueness and K41
sections.summary: Parts XVII-XVIII: Weak-strong uniqueness theorem, Kolmogorov energy spectrum E(k) ~ epsilon^{2/3} k^{-5/3}.
sections.mathContext: Weak-strong uniqueness: if $u$ is a Leray-Hopf weak solution and $v$ is a strong solution with the same data, then $u = v$. K41 spectrum: $E(k) = C_K \varepsilon^{2/3} k^{-5/3}$ in the inertial range $k_f \ll k \ll k_\eta$.

sections.title: Onsager Conjecture and Dissipation Anomaly
sections.summary: Parts XX-XXI: Energy conservation above 1/3 Holder, anomalous dissipation (zeroth law of turbulence).
sections.mathContext: Onsager: $u \in C^{0,\alpha}$ with $\alpha > 1/3$ $\Rightarrow$ energy conserved. $\alpha < 1/3$: non-uniqueness via convex integration (Buckmaster-De Lellis-Székelyhidi-Vicol).

sections.title: Regularity Landscape and Scaling
sections.summary: Parts XXII-XXVI: Regularity criteria survey, dimensional analysis, Prodi-Serrin endpoint, Besov spaces, multifractal structure and intermittency.
sections.mathContext: Prodi-Serrin class: $u \in L^p_t L^q_x$ with $\tfrac{2}{p} + \tfrac{3}{q} = 1$, $q > 3$. Besov criterion: $u \in L^\infty_t \dot{B}^{-1+3/p}_{p,\infty}$ for $p > 3$. Multifractal: singularity spectrum $D(h)$ describes the Hausdorff dimension of the set where the Holder exponent equals $h$.

sections.title: Convex Integration and Singularity Classification
sections.summary: Parts XXVIII-XXX: Non-uniqueness below 1/3 Holder via convex integration, Type I/II singularity classification and dichotomy.
sections.mathContext: Convex integration: for $\alpha < 1/3$, there exist infinitely many weak solutions $u \in C^{0,\alpha}$ with prescribed energy profile. Singularity dichotomy: blowup is Type I ($\|u\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim (T-t)^{-1/2}$) or Type II (faster growth).

sections.summary: Parts XXXI-XXXIII: Stochastic NS with Ito noise, compressible NS (barotropic), critical Sobolev framework H^{1/2}.

sections.title: Fujita-Kato Theory and Blowup Classification
sections.summary: Parts XXXVI-XXXVII: Mild solutions via heat semigroup, Kato existence with quartic scaling, Koch-Tataru BMO^{-1}, minimal blowup solutions, Tao triple-exponential bound.

sections.title: Helicity, Pressure, Liouville Theorems
sections.summary: Parts XXXVIII-XL: Helicity conservation and Beltrami flows, pressure estimates via Calderon-Zygmund, KNSS Liouville theorem, Seregin zero theorem, Landau solution, millennium connection.
sections.mathContext: Helicity: $H(t) = \int u \cdot \omega\,dx$ conserved for inviscid flow. Beltrami: $\omega = \lambda u$ (eigenvectors of curl). Pressure: $-\Delta p = \partial_i \partial_j (u_i u_j)$, with $\|p\|_{L^{3/2}} \leq C\|u\|_{L^3}^2$ via Calderon-Zygmund. KNSS Liouville: bounded ancient solutions in $L^{9/2}$ are zero.

conclusion.summary: This is the largest proof formalization in the gallery: 20,000+ lines, 1200+ definitions/theorems, 0 sorries, across 110 parts. It provides a complete 2D Navier-Stokes proof and conditional 3D regularity (via NSAxioms structure with 5 assumptions), plus comprehensive coverage of modern NS theory including global attractors, determining modes, and exact turbulence results (Kolmogorov 4/5 law).
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Mathematical Significance**

1. **2D Completeness**: The 2D global existence proof is fully verified without any axioms, formalizing Ladyzhenskaya's classical result.
**2. 3D Architecture**: The conditional 3D result demonstrates how the Millennium Problem reduces to excluding two types of singularity (via NSAxioms structure with 5 assumptions).
3. **Theory Coverage**: 110 parts serve as a comprehensive formal reference for modern NS theory: Leray-Hopf, Serrin, CKN, BKM, Fujita-Kato, Koch-Tataru, Onsager, convex integration, global attractors, determining modes, Kolmogorov exact laws, stochastic NS, MHD, and more.
4. **Finite-Dimensional Dynamics**: Part CIX formalizes that NS dynamics is eventually determined by finitely many modes (dim(A) ≤ cG^{2/3}), connecting infinite-dimensional PDE theory to finite-dimensional dynamical systems.
openQuestions: Can the NSAxioms hypotheses be proved from first principles to resolve the Millennium Problem?
Can the CKN partial regularity be extended to show the singular set is empty?
Can the Liouville critical exponent gap (9/2 vs 3) be closed?
Can the stochastic NS formalization be connected to Hairer's regularity structures?

crossReferences.description: The main Navier-Stokes formalization defines the equations and basic properties, while this entry focuses specifically on the Millennium Prize existence and smoothness question — whether smooth solutions exist globally in 3D

Both are Clay Millennium Prize problems concerning PDEs from physics: Navier-Stokes asks about fluid dynamics regularity, while Yang-Mills asks about existence of a mass gap in quantum gauge theory — both remain open

Both are (former) Millennium Prize problems: Poincare was resolved by Perelman (2003) using Ricci flow (a PDE technique), while Navier-Stokes remains open — Ricci flow shares the nonlinear PDE regularity challenges of Navier-Stokes

Hilbert's 19th (regularity of variational minimizers) was resolved by De Giorgi-Nash for elliptic PDEs. Navier-Stokes regularity is the analogous open question for parabolic-hyperbolic Navier-Stokes — the methods overlap but the Navier-Stokes nonlinearity poses additional obstacles

Hilbert's 20th (boundary value problem existence) was resolved via Lax-Milgram for elliptic PDEs. Navier-Stokes existence is the analogous question for incompressible fluid equations — Leray's weak solutions exist but global regularity is unknown

Both are unsolved Clay Millennium Prize problems: BSD concerns L-functions of elliptic curves, while Navier-Stokes concerns fluid dynamics — both represent frontier challenges in their respective fields
